claims.claim: Justin reported close to $450,000 in revenue last year.
claims.quote: Last year I did [snorts] 450,000 close to 450,000.

claims.claim: The business had been operating for 15 years.
claims.quote: And that's what's this that's 15 years ago. 15 years.

claims.claim: The business was 98% commercial.
claims.quote: Um but today it's all 98% commercial.

claims.claim: Justin described a team of three full-time employees plus part-time help, after initially saying four full-time employees.
claims.quote: I have uh four four full-time employees and um I do a lot of well three three to four I'll say three full-time and then you know a couple part-time here and there.

claims.claim: Commercial client payment terms ranged from net 30 to net 120.
claims.quote: With commercial, you're looking at net 30, net 45, net 60, net 90, sometimes net 120.

claims.claim: Before the website work, he might get two calls a year.
claims.quote: I would get two calls a year.

claims.claim: After the website work, he received about eight calls in five or six weeks.
claims.quote: within the last like the last like five or six weeks, I've got about eight calls.

claims.claim: A potential buyer was looking for a company worth roughly $4 million or $5 million.
claims.quote: they would be looking for maybe a four or $5 million company

claims.claim: The host forecast that a salesperson could help the business reach $5 million in revenue.
claims.quote: That's how you're going to get to $5 million of revenue.

claims.claim: The host suggested Justin spend the first six months doing 90% of sales calls alongside a new hire.
claims.quote: maybe the first 6 months you do 90% of the sales calls with this person

claims.claim: The host suggested spending 25% of his time networking and interviewing to find a salesperson.
claims.quote: I would be spending, you know, 25% of my time if I were you just talking to, networking, interviewing people to find that one salesperson.

claims.claim: The host estimated that one good salesperson could double the business.
claims.quote: That's enough to double your business with one good salesperson.

claims.claim: The host asked whether the salesperson would need to sell enough for annual pay of $80,000 or $120,000.
claims.quote: Does this person have to sell a year to make $80,000 or $120,000 or whatever whatever you think uh whatever you think a fair

claims.claim: The host said an experienced salesperson might not work for $50,000.
claims.quote: the best at sales isn't going to come to work for 50 grand 50 grand, you know?

claims.claim: The host gave three trucks breaking down at once as an example of an unexpected business risk.
claims.quote: Three trucks go down at once.

acquisition_channels.details: Early residential work came from paid leads through Service Magic, Home Advisor and Angie's Leads.
Signed up for PlanHub and BuildingConnected and bid on contracts posted there.
Called contractors after bidding to ask about upcoming work and vendor requirements.
A redesigned website began generating calls from people searching for the services.
A commercial client introduced him to other franchise locations and owners.

ideas.delivery: Justin and his employees perform floor care and installation on customer sites; temporary labor is used when projects require extra staff.
